note: In real AWS CloudTrail, digest files contain: (1) SHA-256 hashes of all log files produced in a time window, (2) the SHA-256 hash of the PREVIOUS digest file (to create a chain), and (3) a digital signature generated using AWS's private key. This laboratory version is simplified: it contains hashes of the log files but not the signature, since we do not have AWS's private key. See Section 8(b) for the forensic implications.
note_on_signature: In real AWS CloudTrail, this digest file would be signed using AWS's private key (RSA 2048 bit). The signature would be included as a base64-encoded field. An investigator could verify the signature using AWS's public key (available from https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/cloudtrail-log-file-examples.html#cloudtrail-log-file-digest-file-example), proving that the digest file was genuinely produced by AWS and has not been tampered with. This laboratory version does not include the signature; see Section 8(b) for why this is a forensic problem.
